faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: What you need to know before getting started.

items.question: Will scraping with MediaClaw get my account flagged?
items.answer: MediaClaw works like manual browsing — opening pages, scrolling, and reading visible content. We add randomized delays to mimic natural human rhythm. Platform risk controls target automated high-frequency API requests, not normal browsing patterns. Use MediaClaw at reasonable speeds and your account stays safe.

items.question: Do I need coding skills or API setup?
items.answer: No technical background needed. Install the Chrome extension, open Xiaohongshu or Douyin, and the sidebar appears automatically with context-aware controls. Click 'Start' and wait for the progress bar. No code, no API keys, no proxy configuration — your first scrape takes under 5 minutes.

items.question: Where is my scraped data stored?
items.answer: By default, data stays in Chrome's local storage — nothing is uploaded to any third-party server. If you choose to sync, data goes point-to-point to your private Lark Base table. You control where your data lives.

items.question: Which platforms does MediaClaw support?
items.answer: MediaClaw currently supports both Xiaohongshu (RedNote) and Douyin (TikTok China), covering post/video scraping, comment export, niche opportunity analysis, benchmark account discovery, keyword research, and competitor monitoring for both platforms.

items.question: Is MediaClaw really free?
items.answer: Yes — core scraping features are free forever. The free tier covers the full data collection workflow: scrape posts, collect creator profiles, grab keyword results, store locally, and export CSV anytime. Upgrade when you need comment scraping, competitor monitoring, Lark Base sync, niche opportunity analysis, benchmark account discovery, or in-extension AI capabilities.

items.question: Is it legal to scrape Xiaohongshu and Douyin data?
items.answer: MediaClaw only accesses publicly visible content — the same data any user sees when browsing. We do not bypass login walls, access private data, or use undocumented APIs. Users are responsible for complying with local regulations and platform terms of service when using collected data.
